items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1960-01-03
items.q: Gilda Gray had our debut at the original Vickillain Jazz Band at Follies-Berger New York City

ctx.x: you you stayed over in Europe and then you came back to the states of course and you played music uh all around for for many many years now uh when did you come back home to New Orleans
uh well you would you like me to take the part where I come back to New York and we uh where Gilda Gray had our debut at the original Vickillain Jazz Band at Follies-Berger New York City
in other words 1920 that's when you came back into New York uh but when I came back to New Orleans was in 1925 uh-huh but by that time the Dixieland Band had started to drift apart is that

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: And they only brought Gilda Gray in there to do that dance with us for a showcase.

ctx.x: So now back to Gilda Gray and her shimmy.

Well Gilda Gray did the shimmy and I think she stayed there about maybe two weeks. They put her in there as a sort of showcase so she could get a job in one of the big shows. Well I'll tell you who Gilda Gray was. It was the wife of Gil Bogue. Gil Bogue, Jimmy Thompson and Mr. Salvin owned this Follies Bragé at the top of the Winter Garden. They were the owners of it. Sam Salvin operated as a manager of it. But these other men were the partners. And they only brought Gilda Gray in there to do that dance with us…
Now what did people object to in the dance?

items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: That was when they put Gildegary in jail for doing the shimmy.

ctx.x: Yes that's right. We'll keep it now. This is a letter from Emil Christian and it says I would like Philip Napoleon on cornet and Johnny Costello on clarinet. The boys I was working with because they have more of an idea what I want and they can play all the Dixieland numbers because I'll know we'll get some requests for them. It's signed on the back here. Sincerely, Emil Christian, 2 Bagley Street, Tidingham Court Road, Apartment 1, London, England. And I don't see the date. Let me think. It's on the 1st. The…

Now from this letter you'll see this is a New Orleans man. I could have had him shopping. I could have got him Gardena, Giardina, Tony Giardina was around New York doing nothing. And I had contacted these men finally. But he wanted men who copied from the Dixieland records. We'll go to show you that even the New Orleans boys didn't want the boys from New Orleans because they didn't know the rhythm. That is the truth that I am sitting here and telling you that no New Orleans band played the rhythm that was…

I hate to interrupt you on that story but I missed out a couple of things. I didn't get who was in the band at the time. I know Edwards was back. He replaced Christian and I didn't get the names of the other bands.
